svg.text: Bench breadboard layout: ADS1115 sender interface on a half-size (400-point) breadboard
Built from hardware/WIRING.md and wiring.svg. Hole positions are exact; rail holes are illustrative (any hole on the named strip). Bench only: USB power, no car wiring.
body hangs over the top edge
seen from the back, header on the bottom edge
8-way socket header: push male jumper pins in.
Used: 18 (SCL), 17 (SDA), 3.3V, G. Not used: 16, RX, TX, 5V.
3.3V and 5V are two sockets apart: check before power-on.
USB-C to the laptop powers everything.
a5 … a14 (VDD GND SCL SDA ADDR ALRT A0 A1 A2 A3)
Why these rows: each measurement tap (d17, d21, a25) sits
outside its column's current path, like a Kelvin connection.
Every filter capacitor sits on the ADS1115 side of its 1 kΩ.
Nothing powered: check for shorts between 3V3, GND and every node.
Power from USB; the 3V3 strip reads about 3.3 V (not 5 V).
Flash the normal build: the log must not say 'ADS1115 not responding'.
Rs = 120 Ω. DMM: col 17 to col 21 ≈ 2.63 V (Vp);
Pull Rs out: SENSOR OPEN. Wire b21–b25: SENSOR SHORT.
Bond link j25 → GND becomes 10 Ω: reading unchanged.
Bond link becomes 1 Ω; add the step 8 parts: AA cell
− to h25, + to i27, 27 Ω from j27 to GND (inset). Expect
ground_offset_v ≈ −0.05 V, no fault, reading within 0.2 %.
12 Ω instead of 27 Ω: GROUND FAULT. Remove afterwards.
Swap Rs: 44 Ω, 470 Ω, ~1.2 kΩ (and 4.7 kΩ for #24).
Pull the ground-sense wire (a25): GROUND FAULT.
Step 8 only: around the tank column
(same holes as the main board; everything else stays in place)
dashed = flying leads of the step 8 AA cell (inset only)

• Rails: use the strip nearest row a for 3V3 and the strip nearest row j for GND, whatever colours your board prints; mark them with tape. Some boards split each strip halfway: this layout stays within one half-size board.
• Module: plug it in so each pin lands in the column shown, matching the printed pin names (VDD, GND, SCL, SDA, ADDR, ALRT, A0, A1, A2, A3), not the drawing's shape.
• Measure Rp before fitting it and put the value in kPullUpOhms. Use the same meter for the test resistors.
